newsitem.title: ITALY: San Paolo sale seen raising 4.0 trln lire.
newsitem.headline: San Paolo sale seen raising 4.0 trln lire.

text.p: The forthcoming privatisation of Italy's largest commercial bank Istituto Bancario San Paolo di Torino will bring in some 4.0 trillion lire to the bank's controlling foundation, its chairman Gianni Merlini said.

The foundation, or Compagnia di San Paolo, which indirectly controls 65 percent of the bank, has placed some 20 percent with core shareholders and plans to float 25 percent on the stock market by end-June, leaving it with some 20 percent.
A 35 percent stake in San Paolo was floated in 1993.
"If the privatisation operation all goes well, let's say that four trillion lire is a realistic enough figure, Merlini said in an interview with Turin daily La Stampa.
